convoLines.text: I'm an archive of a world that doesn't exist. Someone should keep the records.
"He lowers the crown. That's Rut King telling you it's about to move. Dawn and dusk, that's when it's out."
"Tell me something you remember about before. Anything. I collect them."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on what they want."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Right. Sorry, I go on about it. What did you want?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Ethan always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
You show them Common Plantain — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"...Hi. Sorry. I'm not good at the talking-to-strangers part."
Something eases in their shoulders. "Oh. Okay. That's... that's fine, then."
"Strangers are just people you haven't disappointed yet. That's what my mother said. Terrible advice, but it got me through parties."
"It rewards understanding, not obedience. Every time someone figures something out, it lights up. It's farming insight, and we're the crop."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on the big questions."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Ethan is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"Sleep's gone strange. I sit apart to eat at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"Did you see that, just now? By the tree line."
"You did?" Their voice drops. "Then I'm not imagining things. Stay close to the fire tonight — both of us."
"This one — Ginkgo Nut. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
You show them Dandelion — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
You walk to the tree line with Jaxon. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on what spooked them."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Good question." "I've told you everything I know about that."
"History isn't what happened. It's what we refuse to let go of. I refuse."
"Right. Go on, then."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"About that question — Do you still count the days? I lost track days ago."
"Good. Keep counting. The days need witnesses."
Their friendliness thins — still there, just held at arm's length.
"Still on what day it is."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Last time things were different. They always are." "Ethan owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"My part? I remember them. Someone has to do it properly."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
You show them Common Plantain — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Sure, let's vote. Democracy always works great with no food."
"I did the count twice. The count doesn't change. Nobody's worked the old burn east of camp in days. We'll fill packs before dark."
"This one — Shepherd's Purse. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"a burned farmhouse — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
There is no playable joint foraging outing yet. Giving food does not perform the promised outing.
"We were just talking. Nothing important."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They took you — The Echo, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"We'll see what the treeline brings. We always do."
"I do the small things right. The big things notice."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"...Actually, forget it."
"About that question — Are you angry? At whoever did this. At the sky. At anything. What's the worst that happens."
"Good. Anger's fuel. Just — point it somewhere useful."
The warmth pulls back a notch. They're weighing something.
"Still on whether you're angry."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? That is all."
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "The Echo. They just... took you. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
You show them Shepherd's Purse — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"My fisherman training covered a lot. 'Post-apocalyptic foraging' was not on the syllabus. I mean it."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Like I said — We were just talking. Nothing important."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Sure — what's on your mind? Funny how that works."
"Good question." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They took Boris — Hardened Duel, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Sure. I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
Dieter: "Hey — come here. You should hear this."
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
Dieter shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"You talk to it -- the System. Have you ever asked? About the taken -- about Sean? No time to waste."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Hardened Duel. They just... took Boris. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on what's been happening."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Can I trust you? I mean really."
"That's the right answer. The wrong one would've been 'yes' too fast."
"Right. Go on, then."
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
